title: Narrow-unit share follows Pvalb-type neuron share across 178 IBL mouse brain regions, better than GABA share, but not across cortical layers or 28 visual-system regions
abstract: We tested if the fraction of narrow-waveform units in a mouse brain region follows the local transcriptomic cell composition. Function data: 56,327 IBL Brain-Wide Map single units (696 insertions, 178 grey-matter regions). Structure data: 2.1 million neurons of the Allen MERFISH atlas brain C57BL6J-638850, registered to the Allen CCF. The narrow-unit fraction (trough-to-peak below 0.40 ms) had a rank correlation of 0.66 (95% insertion and section bootstrap interval 0.60 to 0.69) with the share of neurons in Pvalb-type clusters. This was larger than the correlation with the GABAergic share (0.52; difference 0.14, interval 0.06 to 0.20). The relation also held inside CCF divisions (mean rank correlation 0.31, stratified permutation p = 0.0005), for example in isocortex (0.45), striatum (0.70) and pallidum (0.79). It was negative in the hippocampal formation and olfactory areas. Pvalb types of both transmitter classes predicted equally well. The relation did not generalize everywhere. Across 82 cortical area-by-layer units it reversed (rank correlation -0.21): layer 5 has the most Pvalb-type cells but the fewest narrow units. In the 28 visual-system regions that both datasets sampled, the GABA share predicted at least as well in IBL and in Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels. The two laboratories gave similar regional narrow fractions (rank correlation 0.91). Narrow units were 4 to 150 times more common in odds than Pvalb-type neurons, so most narrow units outside isocortex are not Pvalb cells. Limitations: the composition comes from one MERFISH brain, the tests are correlations between regions, and we did not model detection bias. Code, IBL-derived aggregates, statistics and figures are included. The Allen-derived values are regenerated by script.

display.caption: Each point is one CCF region. Narrow-unit fraction against the MERFISH share of Pvalb-type neurons (left) and of GABAergic neurons (middle) for 178 IBL regions, and against the Pvalb-type share for 29 Allen Visual Coding regions (right). Point size shows the unit count. Colour shows the CCF division.

Left: rank correlations inside each CCF division (IBL). Middle: insertion and section bootstrap distributions of the whole-brain rank correlations and partial rank correlations. Right: isocortex area-by-layer units. Layer 5 has the most Pvalb-type cells but few narrow units, so the across-layer relation is negative.

Logit narrow-unit fraction against logit Pvalb-type share (IBL). The binomial fit (slope 0.57) is above the identity line in all divisions, so narrow units are over-represented relative to Pvalb-type neurons, most strongly in thalamus, striatum, pallidum, pons and hypothalamus.
